claim: IOtA theory: replaying related memories together strengthens shared elements and builds schemas. It is a proposal; no direct test of overlap-weighted replay exists in humans (indirect behaviour plus sleep staging only).
agent_test: none yet; see K20 for the LLM test of overlap sets vs random sets

claim: Slow-wave sleep amount predicting statistical-learning gain (Durrant 2011) was not reproduced in a larger sample (N=69, preprint): SWS predicted no gist type. REM even predicted worse statistical learning (b=-0.626, p=.010, survives FDR).
agent_test: none

claim: In young adults, 8 h of sleep roughly doubles the number who find a hidden rule in the number reduction task (Wagner 2004). The effect is task and age bound: absent in older adults (Debarnot 2017, via review) and absent without initial training.
agent_test: Give the agent a batch of cases with a hidden shared rule; compare an offline consolidation pass vs continued inline search at equal tokens; count rule discoveries.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Sleep effects on hidden-rule extraction are task dependent. Explicit rule detection: 14 of 30 studies found an effect; all 9 stationary-rule explicit tests were null; counting implicit effects too, temporal 31/45 vs stationary 15/22 (the temporal advantage disappears). No pooled effect size exists.
agent_test: Test merge separately on ordered solution traces and on unordered fact sets; expect a gap.

claim: Sleep has no overall effect on DRM false memory (Hedges g=.129, 95% CI -0.282 to 0.539, 13 effects, high heterogeneity). Only recall tests show a sleep rise in false memory (g=.606, CI 0.020-1.192); recognition does not (g=-.150). A 2026 preregistered replication of Diekelmann 2010 also reports no overall effect (snippet only). [Gap search: Nagel et al. 2026 (J Exp Psychol LMC, preregistered, N=398) is a peer-reviewed large DRM replication of Diekelmann 2010: no sleep effect on false memory or general memory. Consistent with the null meta-analysis.]
agent_test: Check merged rules with generation tests, not only recognition (does the agent produce unsupported content that the merge implied?).

claim: Gist can be invisible right after consolidation and appear only after a long delay: in Lutz 2017 sleep raised old-item memory at 10 h but not prototype memory; one year later (N=17) only prototypes encoded before sleep were above chance. Sweegers 2014 found generalisation rose with time regardless of sleep. Matorina found category gist decayed 22% over a week.
agent_test: Evaluate the rule library after many tasks, not after the next one; track per-rule hit rate over 100+ tasks.

claim: Only fully connected relational structure (transitive inference) was retained over a week; overlapping category, summary and statistical sets were not. Ellenbogen 2007 found a sleep gain only on the far pair B>E (93% sleep vs 69-70% wake, n=14 vs 17), with the averaged inference effect null. The larger study concludes overlap is insufficient for long-term generalisation.
agent_test: After a merge, test held-out two-step derived conclusions; gate merges on structure (connected relations), not on surface overlap alone.

claim: New items that fit an existing schema consolidate faster or with less forgetting: rats (Tse 2007, one-trial learning became hippocampus-independent) and humans (Hennies 2016, spindle density plus SWS explained 56.2% of variance in the overnight schema effect; N=19 in regression, correlational).
agent_test: Compare solve rate on new tasks that match an existing rule against tasks that do not; rule-matched tasks should need fewer tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Which sleep stage carries the abstraction effect is unstable: SWS in Lau 2010, REM in Alger and Payne 2016, SWS not at all in Matorina, REM negative there. Stage-specific mechanisms should not be copied into the design.
agent_test: Ablate merge order (within-family then cross-family vs reverse vs single pass) rather than assuming a stage order.
audit_note: Lau 2010 and Alger and Payne 2016 findings were verified only through the Lerner and Gluck review table (secondary); Matorina verified in its preprint.

claim: In artificial networks, interleaved replay of old items with new ones prevents overwriting, and generative or representation replay beats regularisation: Split MNIST class-IL fine-tune 19.90, EWC 19.90, DGR 91.24, RtF 92.56, upper bound 97.93. Sleep-like replay without stored data (Tadros 2022) raises CUB-200 two-task accuracy from 5/95 to 63.2/45.4, but in its own Table 1 it scores below rehearsal with 0.75% stored data on Inc. MNIST, Fashion MNIST and multi-modal MNIST (e.g. 48.47 vs 79.91), and above it on Inc. CIFAR10 (44.55 vs 39.39).
agent_test: When updating the rule library from a new case, interleave it with old cases in the check set; flag any old case that now fails.
audit_note: Tadros Table 1: SRC is below 0.75 percent rehearsal in three of five columns (e.g. 48.47 vs 79.91) but above it on Inc. CIFAR10 (44.55 vs 39.39) and on the CUB-200 average (63.2/45.4 vs 42.32/51.49), so 'scores below rehearsal' is not general.
claim_before_audit: In artificial networks, interleaved replay of old items with new ones prevents overwriting, and generative or representation replay beats regularisation: Split MNIST class-IL fine-tune 19.90, EWC 19.90, DGR 91.24, RtF 92.56, upper bound 97.93. Sleep-like replay without stored data (Tadros 2022) raises CUB-200 two-task accuracy from 5/95 to 63.2/45.4 but in its own table scores below rehearsal with 0.75% stored data (e.g. 48.47 vs 79.91 in the first column).

claim: Replaying solved cases, extracting the fragments they share and adding them as named library primitives raises later solve rate: DreamCoder SyGuS 3.7% to 79.6%; LILO beats DreamCoder (+33.14 REGEX, +20.42 LOGO means); ReGAL up to +11.5% LOGO; AWM +12.0 points (23.5 to 35.5%) on WebArena.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: library of merged subgoals vs raw case retrieval vs no memory, on held-out tasks.
audit_note: DreamCoder's 3.7 to 79.6 percent includes its recognition network as well as library abstraction, and AWM stores workflows rather than named code primitives; numbers are as stated.

claim: Merged abstractions must be named and documented in words. Naive Stitch abstractions changed LILO solve rate by -30.60 (REGEX), -2.91 (CLEVR), -11.11 (LOGO) until AutoDoc gave +9.73, +2.27, +0.00. Only LILO tested this. [Gap search: LILO text deltas mix bases: the REGEX -30.60 is a difference of best-of-3 maxima (90.00 vs 59.40); the mean difference is -22.93. Direction holds on all three domains.]
agent_test: A/B each merged rule with and without a one-line plain-language name and use condition.

claim: Unaided LLM merging is unreliable. LILO: only 19.01% (998/5250) of LLM compressions were valid. ACE: whole-context rewrite collapsed 18,282 tokens to 122 and accuracy 66.7 to 57.1, below the 63.7 baseline. LightMem argues real-time LLM updates wrongly delete compatible facts (worked example only). [Gap search: LILO appendix is the only head-to-head of overlap finders found: Stitch 1.5x to 3.5x compression vs GPT-4 about 1.0x on identical frozen programs, code DSLs only.]
agent_test: Find overlap and do bookkeeping in code; let the model only name, write one slot, or judge a single pair.

claim: Incremental edit merging with de-duplication is used in ACE (grow-and-refine: +10.6% agent, +8.6% finance over strong baselines; its context-collapse case study shows free whole-context rewriting destroyed information; dedup threshold effect non-monotone 77.0/73.9/78.6 at 50/70/90%), ExpeL (ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE with removal at zero) and LightMem (append online, merge offline), but only ACE compares against free rewrite.
agent_test: Log every merge; compare append-only, vote-and-prune, and rewrite at equal tokens.
audit_note: Only ACE contrasts incremental merging with free whole-context rewriting (a single AppWorld case study of context collapse, in a Dynamic Cheatsheet-style rewrite, plus gains over baselines); ExpeL and LightMem are described designs with no head-to-head against free rewrite, so 'works better than free rewrite' rests on one paper.
claim_before_audit: Incremental edit merging with de-duplication works better than free rewrite: ACE grow-and-refine (+10.6% agent, +8.6% finance; dedup threshold effect non-monotone 77.0/73.9/78.6 at 50/70/90%), ExpeL ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE with removal at zero, LightMem append online and merge offline.

claim: Merge only from checked-successful runs, and expect model dependence: AWM fell below no-memory for Claude-3.7-sonnet on WebArena (40.8 vs 41.7) and added 0.9 for Gemini-2.5-pro; ReasoningBank, which also learns from failures, reached 46.3 to 56.3 across backbones; wrong workflows degrade the model.
agent_test: Admit a rule to the library only after it passes a held-out check; measure per base model.
audit_note: 'ReasoningBank reached 46.3 to 56.3' mixes plain ReasoningBank (Claude 46.3) with ReasoningBank plus MaTTS (Gemini-2.5-pro 56.3); plain ReasoningBank spans 46.3 to 53.9. AWM and no-memory figures are exact.

claim: Abstracting sometimes beats storing whole examples and sometimes does not, depending on the task: AWM beat Synapse's whole-example retrieval on Mind2Web (+5.0 element accuracy, +4.0 step success), and ExpeL insights-only beat retrieval-only on HotpotQA (36% vs 31%) but lost on ALFWorld (50% vs 55%). Mind2Web full-task success stays 1-5%.
agent_test: Keep both a rule store and a raw-case store; route by task type and measure which wins.
audit_note: AWM's gain over whole-example retrieval (Synapse) is on Mind2Web, a web-action task, which contradicts 'but not on action tasks'; the ExpeL split (HotpotQA vs ALFWorld) is the only support for the reasoning versus action contrast.
claim_before_audit: Abstracting beats storing whole examples on reasoning tasks but not on action tasks: AWM vs retrieval of whole examples +5.0 element accuracy and +4.0 step success on Mind2Web; ExpeL insights-only 36% vs retrieval-only 31% (HotpotQA) but 50% vs 55% (ALFWorld). Mind2Web full-task success stays 1-5%.

claim: Memory gains depend on the base model but do not simply shrink with model size: Dynamic Cheatsheet gains are mixed for GPT-4o-mini (AIME 2024 16.7 to 13.3 under DC-Cu, AIME 2025 10.0 to 16.7 under DC-RS, GPQA-Diamond flat or down) and for Claude 3.5 Haiku are large on AIME (10.0 to 36.7 and 0.0 to 13.3) but flat on GPQA-Diamond except DC-RS (43.4 to 49.0), and minimal or inconsistent for o1 and R1; ReGAL gives its largest gains to the smallest model tested (CodeLlama-13B), though large models also gain; and a memory built by a stronger model does not reliably help a weaker one (Dynamic Cheatsheet). [Gap search: Dynamic Cheatsheet numbers confirmed (30-question AIME sets). Reversal exists: GRASP strong-writer libraries help weaker executors when gated; weak-writer libraries hurt strong ones; 25% of extractor-target pairs are negative in Huang 2026; skill value does not track model size.]
agent_test: Test the library on the target solver, never only on the model that wrote it.
audit_note: Dynamic Cheatsheet Table 3 shows Claude 3.5 Haiku gaining +26.7 points on AIME 2024 (10.0 to 36.7), as large as Sonnet's, so gains were not small for Haiku (only GPQA-Diamond and GPT-4o-mini were flat or negative); and ReGAL found the smallest model (CodeLlama-13B) benefited most, the opposite of a gains-shrink-with-weak-models pattern.
claim_before_audit: Memory gains shrink or reverse with weak base models: Dynamic Cheatsheet gains small or negative for GPT-4o-mini and Haiku, inconsistent for o1 and R1; ReGAL gains smaller for strong models; a library written by a stronger model does not reliably help a weaker one. [Gap search: Dynamic Cheatsheet numbers confirmed (30-question AIME sets). Reversal exists: GRASP strong-writer libraries help weaker executors when gated; weak-writer libraries hurt strong ones; 25% of extractor-target pairs are negative in Huang 2026; skill value does not track model size.]

claim: Feeding order matters in a merge step: random ordering cut ReGAL LOGO accuracy by 18.7% versus easy-to-hard. [Gap search: ReGAL ablation confirmed: no curriculum LOGO 55.0 to 36.3, Date 77.0 to 56.6, TextCraft 34.12 to 28.78. Three code-like domains, one model, same paper. Not a within-family-first test.]
agent_test: Merge in easy-to-hard, checked-first order vs random order.

claim: Offline computation on stored context pays back when later queries overlap: sleep-time compute about 5x less test-time compute at equal accuracy, up to +13%/+18% accuracy with scaling, 2.5x lower cost per query across related queries; LightMem up to 38x fewer tokens. Benefit tracks query predictability. a23, b20 and c20 are the same paper. [Gap search: Opened: 10,948 generated questions over 1095 contexts (about 10 per context), cost weight t=10, 2.5x per query. No explicit break-even count is in the text.]
agent_test: Run a between-task consolidation pass; count its tokens against the later savings.
audit_note: The 2.5x per-query cost saving is stated for about 10 queries per context; the three Lin et al. lines are one paper, so independent support is Lin plus LightMem.

claim: No opened LLM paper tests the central human claim: merging overlapping items vs merging non-overlapping items, or replay order. 0 direct tests in 22 opened papers (search limited by quota). [Gap search: Still no overlap-vs-random merge test. Nearest: LILO random vs cosine-similarity example selection is mixed (REGEX 77.07 vs 71.33, CLEVR 96.76 vs 97.41, LOGO 48.95 vs 53.15); ReGAL has no random-grouping arm.]
agent_test: Three arms, same solver, held-out tasks: merge by overlap sets, merge random sets, no merge; plus order ablation.

claim: Human replay is structure-guided and salience-weighted: awake replay followed the rule-implied order of new objects (peak 40 ms lag, N=21 and N=22); sleep replay is more frequent for salient or recent items. Evidence is from awake rest or rodent trajectories, not overlap sets.
agent_test: Re-examine solved cases in proportion to value or surprise instead of uniformly.

claim: A skill or rule library helps deep tasks more than shallow ones and benefit grows with train-test distance: Voyager stone tier slower with library (11 vs 9 iterations) while iron 21 vs 29; AWM gap widens from 8.9 to 14.0 points.
agent_test: Gate library retrieval by difficulty; expect no gain on easy items.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Keep episodic cases and gist rules as separate stores with separate retrieval: regularity extraction trades detail for gist (Sweegers 2014), the Schapiro 2017 model has separate pathways for regularities and single episodes (it does not test whether summarising harms episode recall), gist is hippocampus-independent while detail is not (Winocur and Moscovitch 2011), and ACE shows full LLM rewriting of a context can destroy information (one case: 18,282 to 122 tokens). [ExpeL numbers rechecked: insights vs retrieve-only HotpotQA 36 vs 31, ALFWorld 50 vs 55, WebShop 37 vs 38. Routing is by the authors' task type; no learned router found.]
agent_test: Archive raw cases; compare rule-only vs rule+archive when a task needs a specific past detail.
audit_note: Sweegers 2014, Winocur and Moscovitch 2011, ACE collapse (18,282 to 122 tokens, 66.7 to 57.1 vs 63.7 base) and ExpeL numbers (36/31, 50/55, 37/38) check out, but Schapiro 2017 does not simulate summarising or gist extraction or test its effect on episodic recall; it only shows separate pathways learn regularities and individual episodes.
claim_before_audit: Keep episodic cases and gist rules as separate stores with separate retrieval: extraction trades detail for gist (Sweegers 2014), summarising should not damage case recall (Schapiro 2017 model), gist is hippocampus-independent while detail is not (Winocur and Moscovitch 2011), and ACE shows rewrite destroys information. [Gap search: ExpeL numbers rechecked: insights vs retrieve-only HotpotQA 36 vs 31, ALFWorld 50 vs 55, WebShop 37 vs 38. Routing is by the authors' task type; no learned router found.]

claim: Overlap finding works better with explicit structure than with an unaided LLM or plain embedding similarity: shared entities (HippoRAG, +21.3 R@5 on 2Wiki single-step, +3 on MuSiQue, below baseline on HotpotQA), linking before editing (A-MEM ablation, though its links use an LLM), and symbolic top-down compression (Stitch, 3-4 orders of magnitude faster than DreamCoder's compressor; an LLM compressor gave valid abstractions only 19.01% of the time in LILO). Caveat: cosine similarity was fooled by shared surface words in LILO and did not reliably beat random example choice. No head-to-head of entity overlap vs embedding vs symbolic compression exists.
agent_test: Compare entity-overlap, embedding-similarity and symbolic-fragment overlap finders on merge quality.
audit_note: All figures check out (HippoRAG +21.3 R@5 on 2Wiki single-step, A-MEM ablation, Stitch 3-4 orders faster, LILO LLM compressor 19.01% valid, similarity vs random mixed), but the headline 'best done with cheap structure, not the model' is wider than the sources: HippoRAG and A-MEM both use an LLM to build their structure, and the claim itself concedes no head-to-head exists.
claim_before_audit: Overlap finding is best done with cheap structure, not the model: shared entities (HippoRAG, up to +20 R@5 on 2Wiki), linking before editing (A-MEM), symbolic top-down compression (Stitch, 3-4 orders of magnitude faster than DreamCoder's compressor). [Gap search: Caveat: cosine similarity was fooled by shared surface words in LILO and did not reliably beat random example choice. No head-to-head of entity overlap vs embedding vs symbolic compression exists.]

claim: Consolidation can be triggered by a counted signal: Generative Agents reflect when summed importance of recent events passes 150; sleep-time compute benefit tracks predictability. [Gap search: RecMem count trigger: score 81.1 at count 5 vs 78.9 at count 6, 87% fewer tokens (conversation memory). Auto-Dreamer cadence has an interior optimum on ScienceWorld.]
agent_test: Trigger merge when the unmerged-case count or importance sum passes a fixed threshold; compare with fixed-interval merge.

claim: Overlap itself can cause interference: in the sleep-like replay network, overlapping input pixels (12-16 shared) caused forgetting that sleep replay repaired. Overlap is a hazard to manage as well as a signal to exploit; keep an exceptions list beside merged rules.
agent_test: Count old-case failures after each merge; reject merges that break a stored case.

claim: Adding every new item to memory lowers accuracy below a small fixed memory, so admission needs a filter and deletion needs an outcome signal. Xiong 2025: add-all 55.48 vs fixed 67.53 (RegAgent), 13.05 vs 16.75, 32.32 vs 40.11, 59.90 vs 71.50; strict selection 70.95, 38.50, 51.00, 85.40; history-based deletion helped on 3 of 4 agents with a strict judge. GRASP: ungated edits 40.1 vs no-skills 40.6.
agent_test: Admit a merged rule only if it passes a filter; delete rules whose later use correlates with failure.
audit_note: Minor: Xiong strict-evaluator history deletion improved EHRAgent, AgentDriver and CIC-IoT and lowered RegAgent, as claimed; the evidence line's AgentDriver 85.40-to-89.60 label is really CIC-IoT.

claim: A regression gate on stored pass and fail cases is the measured guard against a bad edit breaking an old case. GRASP: no gate 40.1 (K=1) or 63.5 (K=4) vs 88.8 with gate; no regression budget 81.8; probe run but verdict ignored 70.8 and 67.2 (random pick). Same gate added to five baselines raised in-domain by +1.6 to +15.0 but out-of-domain by about 0. No count of bad rules admitted is reported.
agent_test: After a merge, replay the stored cases that used the old rules and reject the merge if more than a small budget of them break.

claim: LLM review of a candidate rule is a weak guard. Huang 2026: an unguided LLM judge picked the better of two skills 46.4% of the time and only 15.8% on pairs with the largest true gap; a rubric lifted it to 73.8% (rubric derived from the same data).
agent_test: Do not accept a merge because it reads well. Use replay results.

claim: Library gains on math can vanish under matched sampling or compute. Berlot-Attwell: TroVE had 3 correct reuses in 3,201 MATH questions and a no-reuse ablation scored equal or higher (number theory 0.290 vs 0.258); LEGO-Prover reused 0 or 1 lemma per split and at matched GPU budget Draft-Sketch-Prove matched or beat it (cost ratio 5.84 to 14.23 per attempt). Two papers by one group, two systems.
agent_test: Any claim that merged rules help on free-text reasoning must beat same-token majority vote and report rule-reuse rate.

claim: Merge timing has an interior optimum and can be count-triggered: RecMem count 5 best (81.1) vs 6 (78.9) with 87% fewer construction tokens; Auto-Dreamer cadence k=1 and k=20 both worse than k=8 or 10 on ScienceWorld. Neither tests rules on reasoning tasks.
agent_test: Trigger a merge when a cluster of 4 to 6 related unmerged cases exists, then re-tune.

claim: Whether a stronger model's library helps a weaker solver depends on gating and domain. GRASP: stronger-writer libraries improved weaker executors, weak-writer libraries hurt stronger ones, and every library moved into FHIR-AgentBench lowered a 51.5 baseline (47.2, 45.7, 48.3). Dynamic Cheatsheet: GPT-4o-mini and Claude 3.5 Haiku gains small or negative. Huang 2026: 25% negative transfer, 47% on ALFWorld. Search snippets (not opened) disagree.
agent_test: Before giving a weak solver a library, test it on stored cases for that solver; keep libraries short.

claim: Time to benefit in agents is measured in tens of tasks, not a year, but early unreadable merges can hurt. AWM gains stabilize within tens of examples (figure note: gap 22.5 after 40 examples); LILO Stitch abstractions without names lowered solve rate on all three domains until documented. No study ran a controlled merge-at-N sweep.
agent_test: Start merging after a few dozen related cases; keep the raw cases until merged rules pass the replay check.

claim: No peer-reviewed large replication of Durrant 2011 (SWS and statistical learning) or Matorina's REM result was found. The N=69 four-gist preprint remains a preprint. The only new peer-reviewed large sleep-gist replication is Nagel 2026 on DRM (N=398), null for sleep. The sleep literature should be read as inspiration, not support.
agent_test: Do not cite sleep results as evidence that merging works; cite the LLM tests.

claim: LLM analogue of DRM false memory is small: critical lure marked old 0.114 vs 0.053 for unrelated words; small local models showed about none (Cao 2025). No study of merged rules causing confident unsupported generation was found.
agent_test: Add an exceptions list and require each merged rule to cite its source cases.
